source: YouTube Data API v3 (Google Cloud) - DONE 2026-09-30 (key in .env; regenerate after pilot, it was pasted in chat)
instructions: Sign in to Google Cloud -> create (or pick) a project -> APIs & Services -> Library -> enable "YouTube Data API v3" -> Credentials -> Create credentials -> API key -> restrict the key to the YouTube Data API v3. Put it in a file named .env at the repository root (git-ignored) as YOUTUBE_API_KEY=<key>. Then run: python scripts/youtube/run_youtube.py plan search --pilot --run <YYYY-MM-DD> (day 1) and: python scripts/youtube/run_youtube.py videos channels comments build sample --pilot --run <same date> (day 2).
why: The YouTube public-recognition pilot cannot run without a key; no HTML scraping is permitted.

instructions: Register (free) at comtradeplus.un.org, subscribe to the "comtrade - v1" free product in the developer portal, copy the primary key into .env as COMTRADE_API_KEY=<key>. The keyed API allows up to 250,000 records per call, which makes HS6 world-export files for the 13 panel countries (needed for HS6 export similarity) feasible. Tell Claude/the pipeline to switch scripts/acquire/acq_comtrade.py to the keyed endpoint (https://comtradeapi.un.org/data/v1/get/C/A/HS).
why: The keyless preview caps 500 records/call and throttles after ~190 calls; HS6 overlap measures need the keyed API (or BACI, task C2).

source: Harvard Growth Lab - International Trade Data (HS92) on Harvard Dataverse
instructions: Open the DOI, click "Access Dataset" -> download these files individually, completing the guestbook form when asked: hs92_country_product_year_6.csv (1.0 GB), hs92_country_year.csv, hs92_product_year_6.csv, hs92_data_dictionary.csv. Optional (large): hs92_country_country_product_year_6_2010_2019.csv and _2020_2024.csv for HS6 bilateral flows. Also download growth_proj_eci_rankings.csv from doi:10.7910/DVN/XTAQMC and product_hs92.csv from doi:10.7910/DVN/3BAL1O.
why: HS6 country-product exports for export-similarity robustness; the API was used for HS4 only. The guestbook form is a terms/identity step we do not bypass.

source: Korean outward FDI - small partners / full country table (Korea Eximbank) and UNCTAD bilateral FDI
instructions: PARTLY DONE: the quarterly reports on data.go.kr (dataset 3040164, pointed out by the PI) were downloaded automatically and parsed for 2015-2025 (major destinations only). Remaining: (a) Korea Eximbank: 해외투자통계 -> 국가별 -> select all years (1980-latest), all countries, amounts on both 신고(declared) and 투자(invested) basis -> export Excel. Repeat for 국가별 x 업종별 if available. (b) UNCTAD Bilateral FDI Statistics 2014 (covers 2001-2012): https://unctad.org/topic/investment/investment-statistics-and-trends -> "Bilateral FDI statistics" -> download the Excel files for Korea, China, Viet Nam, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Brunei (keep the file names as listed on the page).
preferred_filename: koreaexim_odi_by_country_<years>.xlsx; UNCTAD files keep original names
why: OECD BMD4 by counterpart starts ~2005 and has suppressed cells; Korean-reported ODI goes back to 1980. unctad.org returns HTTP 403 to automated clients.

instructions: Indicator "Patent applications" -> Report type "Total count by applicant's origin" (and "Resident applications per country of origin") -> select the 13 panel countries (+JPN, USA) -> years 1980-latest -> Export CSV. Repeat for "PCT international applications by origin" and, optionally, "Patent applications by technology field" (35 WIPO fields).
why: WDI already holds resident/non-resident applications (WIPO-sourced); PCT and technology fields add capability detail.

instructions: Log in to data.go.kr -> search "관세청 국가별 수출입실적" / "관세청 품목별 국가별 수출입실적" -> 활용신청 (apply) -> store the service key as KCS_API_KEY=<key> in .env. Only needed for monthly or HSK 10-digit Korean data. (Dataset ids were not verified here - pick the 관세청 provider entries.)

source: Korean Diplomatic White Papers 1990-2025 - OCR of scanned editions (LibreOffice part DONE 2026-10-02)
url: data/interim/text/white_papers_index.csv (status per file); raw PDFs in data/raw/kr_mofa/2026-09-30/white_papers/
instructions: Text corpus built for 183 files (1998-2008, 2011-2017, 2019, 2021-2025; LibreOffice converted old HWP/.doc). Remaining: 105 image-only PDFs (status needs_ocr) for 1990-1997, 2009, 2010, 2018, 2020, plus 6 zip members from 1999-2000 that failed conversion. Either approve installing Tesseract OCR with Korean data (winget UB-Mannheim.TesseractOCR + kor.traineddata) so Claude can OCR them, or OCR them yourself (e.g. Acrobat "Recognize text") and save OCR'd copies as NEW files.
file: OCR'd PDFs or text (never overwrite the originals)
why: Completes the only official ANNUAL text series back to 1990 (pre-1998 editions are all scans).
